resale_co.name: Residential Certificate of Occupancy (Resale or Change of Ownership)
resale_co.lead_time: Must be obtained before settlement; the office calls to schedule the inspection once the application is approved (no number of days published; the code says inspection within five working days of the application)
requirements: House number visible from the street, at least 4 inches tall
Steps without trip-hazard cracks; open wood risers closed so a 4 inch ball cannot pass
Cracked sidewalk or walkway blocks with a change in elevation must be replaced
Guardrails (36 inch minimum) where porches, landings or stairs are over 30 inches above grade; handrail on steps with 4 or more risers
Yard free of high grass, weeds, debris and bamboo (unless contained per Borough code)
Grading slopes away from the foundation; gutters, downspouts and splash blocks in place
Sump pump crock must have a pump, check valve, proper outlet, and discharge outside (never to the sanitary sewer)
No signs of pests; if found, a licensed pest control certification is needed
Bathroom window or exhaust fan; GFCI protection on existing bathroom, kitchen counter, garage and exterior outlets
Electrical covers, fixtures and panel secure and labeled; A/C disconnect at the outdoor unit
Bedroom windows open easily for escape; no double-keyed deadbolts
Water heater with proper relief valve and discharge pipe to 2 to 6 inches above the floor; no leaks
Heating system working
Smoke alarms on each floor including basement (10-year sealed battery); CO alarms near bedrooms if there is a gas or oil appliance
ABC fire extinguisher no larger than 10 lbs within 10 feet of the kitchen (form still lists it)
Work done without permits and open permits must be resolved

fees.label: Resale CO inspection (cash or check only)

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Application for Certificate of Occupancy for Residential (check 'Single Family Dwelling RESALE') and bring or mail it (addressed 'Attn: Construction') to the Construction Office, 21 E. Browning Road, Bellmawr, with exact cash or a check payable to Borough of Bellmawr. All taxes, grass cuts, liens and open permits must be paid or closed before the application is accepted. The office calls to schedule the inspection once approved. Inspections are by lockbox or a 2 to 3 pm or 3 to 4 pm window. After passing, email to request the certificate or pick it up from the bin outside the Construction Office.
resale_co.contact_title: Certificates of Occupancy, Housing & Rental (also Mike McDonough, Certificates of Occupancy, Housing & Rental Inspections)

evidence.quote: Must be obtained prior to settlement.
CO’S ARE VALID FOR 30 DAYS OF ISSUANCE
This cert is for every time a home changes ownership.

All buildings or structures used, occupied or offered for occupancy as dwelling units or as apartments on a lease or rental basis shall be inspected by the Construction Official or his representative on every initial occupancy, change in ownership or change of occupancy after the effective date of this article.
Fire Extinguisher - The extinguisher should consist of an ABC type, rated no larger than 10lbs and be located within 10 feet of the kitchen area.

resale_co.notes: Re-checked 2026-10-20; the CO page, the application (April 2026) and the Home C.O. Inspection Checklist (April 2026) are unchanged in substance. Authority: Borough Code Chapter 341, Property Maintenance, Section 341-13 (inspection on every change in ownership; no owner, agent or broker may sell, rent or lease a dwelling unit without a certificate of occupancy), read on ecode360 through its print view. The code fee section (Chapter 210) points back to Chapter 341 and does not list a separate amount, so the page fees are used. The application also has a 'Change of Ownership ONLY' option: no inspection, valid 30 days, but no one may occupy the property until a full CO is issued. Buying a property that is already a rental or duplex is treated as a resale. Rental tenant changes are a separate program. Published inspection days differ: the CO page says Tuesdays and Thursdays, the application says Monday to Thursday, and the staff listings say Monday/Thursday (Greg Conti) and Tuesday/Wednesday (Mike McDonough). The Borough checklist still lists a fire extinguisher, while the Fire Department smoke/CO form says it is no longer required since February 2025.

requirements: Smoke alarms must match the rules in effect when the house was built (hardwired and interconnected in newer homes); hardwired alarms cannot be replaced with battery units
Smoke alarms no more than 10 years from date of manufacture; 10-year sealed battery where battery alarms are used
Smoke alarm within 10 feet of every bedroom door; basement alarm within 10 feet of the stair opening
Alarms mounted with proper hardware; nails, tacks, tape or Velcro not accepted; 3 feet from fan blades and HVAC vents
CO alarm outside sleeping areas, no more than 10 feet from any bedroom
Monitored alarm systems in homes built 1977 or later must be kept working
Secondary power source label within 18 inches of the main electrical panel and meter (generator, solar panels, battery storage)
Fire extinguisher no longer required for the smoke/CO certificate as of February 2025 (per Fire Department form)

authorities.how_to_apply: Fill out page 1 of the Bureau of Fire Prevention Certification of Smoke Detector and Carbon Monoxide Alarm Compliance application and return it with a check or money order payable to Borough of Bellmawr (no refunds). Pay separately from the CO fee. Office: 21 E. Browning Road; Fire Marshal's Office 856-933-1313 ext. 1239.

evidence.quote: Certification of Smoke Detector & Carbon Monoxide Alarm Compliance

As of February 2025, due to a change in the New Jersey Uniform Fire Code, a fire extinguisher is no longer required in residential properties when obtaining a Certificate of Smoke and Carbon Monoxide Alarm for a change of ownership or tenancy.
Please note: CO payment and Fire payment must be submitted as separate payments.

fire_cert.notes: The Borough CO page now links the smoke/CO form as DocumentCenter/View/1562 (same file as the View/1564 link used before; dated April 10, 2026). Conflicting Borough statements remain: the CO page says 'No separate fire/smoke - all in one (see checklist).', yet it links the Fire Department's separate smoke/CO application with its own fee schedule, and the CO application says CO and fire payments must be separate. Most likely both are requested together but paid separately. The DCA fire directory (survey 5/26/2026) lists Fire Official Robert T Fowler with the smoke detector compliance contact as 'Bellmawr Boro Constr Office', 21 E Browning Rd, (856) 933-1286. Inspectors: Patrick Slemmer (Fire Inspector 3-A) and Shawn Fanslau (Fire Inspector 3-B).

other_items.label: Taxes, grass cutting charges and liens paid first
other_items.detail: All charges (taxes, grass, liens, etc.) must be paid before the CO application is accepted, even if they would be paid at settlement. Call 856-933-1313.

other_items.label: Open permits and vacant property fees
other_items.detail: Any vacant property fees and open permits must be closed out before any certificate is issued.

open_questions: Is the smoke/CO certificate truly separate from the CO (separate Fire Department form and payment) or folded into the CO inspection ('all in one')? Confirm with the Construction Office (856-933-1286) or Fire Marshal (856-933-1313 ext. 1239).
Does the Construction Office still check for a fire extinguisher at resale (its checklist lists one; the Fire Department form says it is no longer required)?
